head: working-tree
subject: gRPC xDS fail_on_data_errors
change: runtime.Options.fail_on_data_errors implements the gRPC xDS server feature. When a SotW or delta LDS/RDS/CDS/EDS/SDS resource fails typed validation, its cached listener, route tree, cluster, endpoint assignment or secret is dropped and the removal is published; the response is still returned as an error so the caller NACKs it. The invalid resource's name is recovered leniently from protobuf field 1 when decoding fails before the name is consumed. Without the option the previous cached resource is retained (default behavior).

tests.unit: src/grpc/xds/runtime/fail_on_data_errors_tests.zig covers SotW CDS, delta CDS, SotW EDS, SotW SDS, SotW LDS, SotW dynamic RDS, delta LDS and invalid RDS for an inline listener: each drops the cached resource where applicable, publishes the removal and still returns the decode error; old projection epochs keep endpoints until the next synchronization prunes them. src/grpc/xds/raw_name.zig covers lenient name extraction from truncated payloads.

focused_gate.command: zig build test-lib -Dtest-filter='xDS runtime' -Dtest-filter='gRPC CDS' -Dtest-filter='gRPC LDS' -Dtest-filter='SDS' -Dtest-filter='LRS' -Dtest-filter='fail_on_data_errors' --summary all

test_hardening: The WSS and HTTP/2 server caller-timeout tests now accept transport-close errors from deliberately late handshakes (ConnectionClosed, UnexpectedEof, EndOfStream, PeerClosed, LocalClosed), because the assertion is that the server enforced the shared TLS+HTTP budget. This removes the recurring full-suite flakes caused by host load without weakening the timeout assertion.
notes: A response containing both valid and invalid resources applies the valid subset and drops the invalid names, matching grpc-core's per-resource handling. resource_timer_is_transient_error remains a status-only difference and is still unimplemented.
